walkthroughs.body_html:
UK in the 21st Century — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

UK in the 21st Century brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with UK in the 21st Century.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In a tropical rainforest nutrient cycle, where is most of the nutrient stored?
options: Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
Most nutrients in a rainforest are stored in the soil — that's why plants grow so well.
Ice ages happen every winter when it gets cold.
In the biomass (living plants). Litter is rapidly decomposed by warm humid conditions, and soil is leached — so cycling between biomass and litter dominates.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an ice age and a glacial period?
options: Ice ages happen every winter when it gets cold.
An ice age is a long era with permanent ice on Earth (we are still in one); within it, glacial periods (cold) alternate with interglacials (warm) every ~100,000 years driven by Milankovitch cycles.
The ice age ended 10,000 years ago.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
A corrie is just a small lake at the top of a mountain.

Snow accumulates in a north-east-facing hollow, compacts to ice, and rotational movement combined with plucking and abrasion deepens the hollow into an armchair shape; meltwater can fill it as a tarn.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
A corrie forms when a river dries up high in the mountains.
